I have no one to blame but myself for this one. I read and didn't like book one. I bought Book 2 because, well, I'm stupid. 
 This book was worse that the first. A little bit more sex, nothing awesome though. And Oh. my. god. the writing was terrible. The random italics. The over use of using.periods.to.stress.a.point. Totally distracting and pointless. And the whole texging eacher other song titles and lyrics, cute idea, if you are FIFTEEN. 
 This book goes like this: 
 She runs back to him, he pushes her away again, she runs back to him, he pushes her away again, she runs back to him, he pushes her...think you got it? 
 Please, writers, STOP with the weak women and rich/powerful broken man story line. Normal men can be sexy and freaky in the bedroom. Not all women have to be doormats. 
 I will again state that Rylee's backstory is heartbreaking and a new twist on a familiar story, but that's where the good ends and the rest is just, meh. 
 ETA: 
 I forgot to mention, writing several chapters from Colton's point of view didn't really work for me with this book. It can work, but for some reason it just didn't work for me here. It was distracting and honestly, he came across as kind of dumb. I didn't really get the "powerful rich man vibe" from him. Just more like "dumb jock".
Entirely too much fu**ing repetition in this book. Not to mention entirely too much use of every variation possible of the work fu**! The unnecessary language detracted from the story.

Kurzbeschreibung 
 Nachdem Rylee und Colton sich bei einer Wohltatigkeitsauktion kennen gelernt haben, sind beide nach einem Katz und Maus spiel zusammen. 
 Allerdings nicht so wie sich Rylee das vorgestellt hat, denn Coltons Damonen aus der Vergangenheit sind noch sehr prasent. 
 Beide mussen versuchen einen Weg zu finden aus alten Zwangen... 
 Cover 
 Das Cover ist wie schon vom ersten Teil sehr gut als Titel der Reihe zu erkennen, und bis auf den Titel und eine andere Darstellung der Protagonisten mit demselben tollen Schriftbild in Pink mit weisser Schrift. Fur mich sehr passend zum Inhalt und harmonisch gestaltet. 
 Charaktere 
 Rylee Thomas ist eine ganz liebe, kann aber auch stur sein, was ihr aber nicht ganz so einfach fallt, denn Rylee ist sehr gefuhlvoll und mitfuhlend. 
 Colton Donovan hat Damonen aus seiner Vergangenheit und ist es gewohnt keinen in seine Nahe zu lassen und wenn dann nur zu seinen Bedingungen. 
 Schreibstil 
 Die Autorin K. Bromberg hat einen tollen flussigen Schreibstil der einen sehr schnell in den zweiten Teil entfuhrt der sehr viel uber die Beziehung der beiden verrat und man eine Achterbahn der Gefuhle erlebt. Bildhaft und emotional... ;) 
 Meinung 
 Wenn dich Deine Vergangenheit einholt.... 
 Dann sind wir bei Rylee und Colton angekommen, die sich von ihren Gefuhlen in einem Sturm befinden der nur die beiden zur Ruhe bringen konnen. 
 Aber Colton hat mit seinen inneren Damonen zu kampfen und schiebt Rylee von sich weg indem er ihr sagt dass er sie nur gebraucht hat und jetzt wegwirft wie ein altes Handtuch. 
 Aber Rylee lasst sich nachdem der erste Schock uberwunden ist nicht so behandeln und bekommt sehr schnell mit das vor ihr ein anderer Colton steht. 
 Nicht der taffe selbstsichere Geschaftsmann sondern ein kleiner Junge innerlich der tief verletzt wurde und nie uber diese Traumata hinweg kam. 
 Sie beschliesst ihm eine Chance zu geben und Colton muss sehr bald feststellen das diese Beziehung nicht auf seinen Regeln besteht sondern das hier nur ein miteinander herrschen kann. 
 Aber auch fur Rylee ist es schwer denn sie muss Colton die Stirn bieten obwohl sie nichts lieber tate als ihn zu sehen und ihn zu fuhlen. 
 Unterstutzung und Zuspruch bekommt Rylee von Haddie die ihr mit Rat und Tat zur Seite steht, und somit beginnt fur beide eine Zeit in der sie beide aufeinander zugehen mussen. 
 Aber das Schicksal hat noch vieles parat fur beide. Denn Coltons Eifersucht und sein Besitzanspruch an Rylee sind sehr ausgepragt.... 
 Fazit 
 Sehr empfehlenswert fur mich wie schon der erste Teil und ich freue mich schon auf den dritten. :D 
 5 von 5 Sternen

This book was intense!! I had to stop for a while, because I just couldn't take it and had to give myself a break. When I started again, I was mad at Colton. Then I wanted to kick some sense into Rylee, then I could understand why she was acting the way she was. And like everyone else, I can't stand Tawnee! This book is so amazing. I loved this love story! The characters are so well-developed. I read all three of the books of this series and I was able to read each book in one sitting. Two words: READ THEM!!!

OMG that was f***ing awesome. 
 Gahhhh....when does No3 come out??????

OMG where the hell do I start. 
 Until a couple of nights ago I hadn't read Driven, which I got stuck into and could not put down only to be so relieved I had an ARC of Fueled to jump straight into. 
 I love Colton and how possessive he is with Rylee and how he couldn't stay away no matter how much he tried. 
 This books starts with a prologue written from Colton's POV showing what was going through his head during the last scene of Book 1, Driven and I was so relieved that it jumped straight in the way it did in Chapter 1. 
 Throughout the book there are up's and downs in true Colton fashion, but thanks to Colton's best friend things work out. 
 One minute I wanted to cry and the next I was laughing 'Roses are Red' OMG so funny. My poor heart didn't know whether to stay in my chest or jump right out!! 
 I was so relieved K Bromberg didn't make him unfaithful to Rylee, not sure I could have handled that one. Yeah I want a happily ever after which I guess we won't get until book 3, but I wanted to cry at the end of Fueled and just need crashed to be happy again. 
 If I could I'd give these books 10* they are that good, and coming from me who refuses to read books with cliffhangers, that's saying something.

Once again K. Bromberg races it off the tracks. I cannot wait until my book allowance allows me to finish this series. Colton & Becks have definitely been added to my collection of "book boyfriends"!!!
The ending killed me!! I love this series! Colton can be so sweet one moment and an ass the next!

Fueled is book #2 in K. Bromberg's trilogy. After screaming my head off because I didn't know that Driven ended with a massive cliffhanger I dove straight into this book and I was not disappointed!! The story continues with the burgeoning romance between Colton and Rylee. There is a lot of angst in this book as well as Colton continues to pursue Rylee. In this book a lot of Colton's past conquests rear their ugly heads and cause Rylee to feel insecure about herself. We learn a lot more about the incidents from both Rylee and Colton's pasts. Can they overcome their own inner demons caused by their pasts to find a way to each other? This story spends a great deal of time focusing on the house that Rylee works with and I dare anyone who reads this book not to fall in love with all of the boys in the house, especially Zander. This poor boy has been traumatized so badly he doesn't speak and can barely interact with anyone. But Colton seems to be one person that Zander attaches himself to and the interactions between these two just melts your heart as well as Rylee's. 
 Fueled is a definite roller coaster ride of emotions and you go through hell and back with Rylee who has finally admitted her feelings for Colton. It's one step forward two steps back throughout this book. But man what a ride it is! Jealously and insecurities play a big part in this book. I will fully admit that I want to scratch the eyes right out of Tawny's head! Maybe right after I throat punch her! Tawny is an old friend of Colton's who he has dated in the past and now works for him. Trust me when you read these books you will want to do the same to her. 
 This book is a must read and one I will read over and over again along with Driven. I am so anxious for book #3 to come out!

Holy batman, Spider-Man. This book was a freaking train wreck. These two drove me bananas BUT I loved their ridiculous over the top drama filled fights. I wanted to beat them both up at times. HA! I was entertained but still not sure if will continue on with book 3. It was hella better than book 1 though. Their narrative was still blah (skimmed) but as a whole I liked it.
This is the second book in the Driven trilogy. Did no disappoint. The ending was OMG. Cant wait for book three.

OMG I absolutely love this book!!I'm way to hooked with Rylee and Colton's history there's so much going on that I can't help it. 
 I have to admit that I almost die with the whole crash thing, Jez thank God I knew about the third book or I for sure would thought that he was going to die. 
 Rylee is way to strong, both are amazing characters and very deep, but I usually tend to don't like the girl character cuz they always are so annoying and clingy but no Rylee, how she fights for Ace is impressive, specially when you wouldn't blame her if she wanted to run
I skip read some of this book because it seemed that the plot was moving too slow.

I loved the fact that I could go straight to book 2, and Colton is starting to open up. His story is heartbreaking. I did find myself rolling my eyes at times and skim reading as they seemed to have the same argument but I think that was how you were supposed to feel. Again I couldn't put this book down.
I am still struggling with this series. I like the story but at the same time I am not sure. I wish they would just get their act together and figure their shit out.

I hate being right. 
 it makes me think I read too much. and can i just just point out to budding authors out there.. you don't need to scream every time you have an arguement. in fact most arguement never reach screaming level, cause that's pretty violent and cops get called

Holy mother fucking cliffhanger! I mean really. THAT WAS FUCKING BRILLIANT! I know I'm late to the party - people have been telling me to read these books for a while now. Well no freaking wonder! I want to kick myself in my own ass for not listening! 
 My chest hurts after that. I physically freaking ache over the ending of this damn book. 
 I read Driven and Fueled back to back, I really liked Driven (4 stars for me) but Fueled is on another planet. You are pummeled with angst from the very first page and it never lets up. Colton's inner turmoil is fucking heartbreaking. If anyone in this lifetime ever needed a damn hug, it's him. 
 "Spiderman. Batman. Superman. Ironman." 
 Are you fucking kidding me? How am I ever supposed to view those superhero characters in a normal way ever again? I mean holy shit, those 4 words alone will forever make my heart ache. 
 I feel like I'm going through stages of grief over this book. First I was shocked. And then I cried. And now I'm pissed and want to know what the hell happens next?! 
 And the ending. Sweet baby jesus. That ending will be hard for anyone to ever top. I LOVE a good cliffhanger, I love the shock and awe of it. I love to feel like I've been slapped upside the head by an unexpected ending. Fueled hurt my heart. Made me freaking cry. I feel fucking lost now. 
 BEST CLIFFHANGER EVER! 
 **** 
 Updated: 
 I was so overwhelmed by the damn ending that I totally forgot to mention how much the sex in this book rocked. 
 I think I'm done now. 
 Maybe. 
 I'm a mess over this damn book.
uhmm! I am so emotional right now. book 3 I need it now! Goodness this book was very hectic I think my blood pressure is sky high lol. It was great though I seriously can't wait for the next book.
OMG - it's even better. Colton I race you too;-) bring on Crashed!!!
All about Colton's demons... and breaking down walls.. loved it loved it!!! The damn cliffhanger though!! I'm dying!!! Onto Crashed now...
Never boring and truly passionate!

Wow!! I love it when sequels are just as good, if not better than the first! Fueled definitely falls into that category. These two are such great characters!! There is a lot of back and forth. *3.5 - 4 Stars* 
 So Im having a slight dilemma on how to rate and review this book - its obviously captivating and intriguing because I essentially read it in one sitting but Im just not 100% sold. 
 I think my main issue is the whiplash I'm constantly feeling with them. One minute they're saying and doing one thing and a sentence later they're doing the complete opposite!! Its hard to respect Rylee when she has no resolve. 
 But I do like them, I just dont love them. I like Colton's character and even Rylee's to a point but theyre just not a favourite. 
 I will note that I immensely enjoy the topic of the book - with the kids and the home and Colton's back story. Its definitely refreshing and I care about the kids portion of the story as much as Im invested in Colton and Rylee's story. 
 With the cliffhanger endings its a definite addicting read!

3.5-4 stars. Finally some fuel, pun intended, to the story. Had a tough time with the repetitiveness of the first I would say half of the story, but then it got so much better! Rylee gave Colton a "ride" for his money and good on her!! Loved the fact that she sucked up her tears and made him accountable for his actions or lack there of! On to book 3!!
I can't believe she did it again....I'm dying here!!!!!!!!!! Arghhhhhhhh....I need the next book ASAP!!!!!!!!!

Where do I begin? Fueled by K. Bromberg was the kind a book you want to crawl up with and get lost in. Rylee and Colton still do that thing they do. She pushes and he ends up pulling away. This is way more emotional then Driven. It will definitely hit that spot in your heart that you can't forget about. This time around Rylee is more accepting of Colton and his indiscretions. She wants to be with him and she is willing to accept the whole package. K. Bromberg definitely outdid herself, I didn't think it could possibly get better then Driven. I was wrong this book has blown me away! 
 First off if you haven't read book one in the series then stop here and go read it like right now. Fueled picks up exactly where Driven ended. Yes you have to experience that heart wrenching ending again, but it's all good. Rylee doesn't let Colton push her away this time. She goes back to him and gives him what he needs. What happens between them is simply beautiful. I can't even put into words the emotions I felt. I am still reeling from it and it's been a few weeks since I finished reading the book. In this book Rylee and Colton discover what they mean to one another. Rylee falls madly in love with Colton she is determined to show him in any way possible what he means to her. The only thing Colton knows is that he can't and won't let Rylee go. She drives him crazy, she makes him feel things he never thought possible. They are simply explosive together. It doesn't get better then what they have. Nothing is easy for them. They both have to work hard to be with one another. There are people determined to keep them a part. It seems Tawny is still in the picture. She is relentless when it comes to getting Colton's attention, and ylee isn't going to fight with all she has for Colton. I wouldn't expect anything less from Rylee. She is sweet and innocent on the outside, but on the inside her heart has had enough. She is a fighter and giving up is not an option. 
 I can't tell you enough how much I connected with this story and it's characters. This by far has to be one of the best books I have read this year. I feel so engrossed in this story that I can't stop thinking about how extraordinary the love between Rylee and Colton is. It makes me, happy, mad, and sad all at the same time. I am so in love with Rylee and Colton! I am invested in their happily ever after if ever one exists for them. 
 This is a must read. I want to shout from the rooftops for anyone to hear how wonderful this series is. I am so ready for the conclusion to their story. It can't come soon enough. My recommendation is a no brainer stop what your doing and get to it. You may have to join a support group for your ever huge book hangover. It will definitely be worth it though.

Well book two read and this one was better than book one. This one is full of developing feelings, angst, and sorrow. I was really devouring through every word of the angst trying to get to something anything that would let me breathe again. So very glad that I already have book three because if I was waiting months for it to come out to read what happens next I would be crushed. I am rushing off now to book three.

Usually the second book is never as good as the first, but that is NOT the case with Fueled. I almost liked this one more than the first. This book is not roses and butterflies. It's hard to read at times and it breaks your heart. It's like watching your 2 best friends fight against loving each other and hurting each other and you can't do anything about it. Kristy makes you feel their pain and she makes you part of the story and part of the fight. You are hurt when they are apart and you are cheering when they are together. The sex is off the charts hot and steamy! I caught myself yelling at my kindle and when it was over I closed the cover and hugged it and sighed. Seriously. And as other reviewers have said it does turn you into a facebook/goodreads stalker. But, Kristy loves her fans and it's worth it :) All the fangirls are proud to admit it!

The story of rylee Thomas and Colton Donovan continues... 
 This book was so much better than the first

Love love love it. I read the Driven series when it first came out, and am still in love with Colton and Rylee
Loved, loved, loved. Not sure if I loved it more or less than #1....maybe more for some reasons, less for others. Either way, LOVED it! Can't wait to read CRASHED!
2.5...still eye roll inducing and yet I can't help but move on to book 3.

This series has it's ups and downs for me. At times I'm like seriously.. I don't like how the rylee doubts herself at times and her annoying insecurities. I don't like how Colton sometimes talks (more the third then second maybe because of his povs it's just the random swear words sound so out of place) but I still love this book and series. I love more intense romances and this would be one of them. Amazing book Colton is everything. I also loved the parts where they were fighting and screaming things at each other I couldn't help but laugh

Colton outshines in this second installment of the Driven Trilogy by making a tremendous effort in his turbulent relationship with Rylee. He is courageous in the shadows of his creeping memories. He becomes a hero worth rooting for. 
 Rylee, on the other hand, is the sum of everything I despise in a leading lady. She's unattractively catty, immature, passive-aggressive, whimper-y, and avoids communication in lieu of running off her mouth. She doesn't listen. She runs away. Always running. Always whimpering. 
 The conflict is wholly based on a misunderstanding, made worse by Colton and Rylee's failure to discuss it. Would there have been a story if she'd just shut up and let him talk? No, but the constant relationship drama and the pages and pages of spiteful bickering keeps you engaged in a nerve-shredding, spit-flinging, positively frustrating way. Especially when you already know how things will end. You'll predict the cliffhanger chapters in advance. Everything about this story is predictable, because there's nothing unique here. 
 But I loved it. When I was forced to put the book down, I did so relunctantly. Maybe it's the evocative way it's written. Maybe it's all the raw heat blazing between Colton and Rylee, and the hot, hot, scorching hot sex scenes. Maybe it's the merciless drive to screw with your emotions until you're ready to become a beserker right along with the characters. Whatever it is, it puts you through the wringer and turns you into a glutton for more messy emotional chaos. 
 So, while this book is a compilation of all my peeves (cliffhanger, cliches, unlikeable heroine, contrived conflict), Colton and his drama penetrates and hooks. His aboutface will charm you, warm you, and make you care about what happens to him. I'd put up with the most unsavory of heroines just to spend more time with Ace.
I'm not sure that I can handle the suspense of waiting for the third book! This book kept me locked in just as the first one did!

I was so happy when things seemed to be working out at the end of the book. I love Colton and Rylee. I've laughed and cried while reading this series. Hopefully we won't have to wait too long for Crashed. Love this series.
I loved it!! I would love to give this book 10 stars!! Can not wait for Crashed!!

4.5 "Spiderman. Batman. Superman. Ironman." "My spark." Kisses 
 So...I can't lie, I was mad at Colton when I read the last few paragraphs of 
 Driven 
 . Did the Prologue of Fueled make me feel a little shitty for that? Oh heck yes....but after I got through that, suffered through the emotional torment of Ryles and Colton...and then read the last few paragraphs of Fueled...I'm back to being pissed again! WTF K. Bromberg?!!?!? 
 Rylee Jade...damn it I love this girl. I want to hug her for about 5 minutes solid and then go out for drinks because she is so freakin relatable, it's scary. She's brave and sassy but still has that glimmer of insecurity and fear that all women have. She's compassionate and smart and freaking real. I connected with her even more over the course of this book. She just squeezed my heart so much, I felt every emotion, her happiness and glee, her sadness and devastation...it was such a rollercoaster, I'm mentally exhausted. She made me cry...almost as much as Colton did. I'm an emotional reader and when I connect with a heroine as much as I connected with Rylee, it's really hard for me to disconnect myself...so the entire tumultuous journey that she just experienced, I was right there with her, holding her hand. GAH!!! I just can't even tell you. 
 "I don't think I could ever get my fill of you." Proving my point exactly. Words that say it but don't really say it. "You're always so reserved, but when I'm in you..." he shakes his head, a low hum deep in his throat "...you lose all sense of everything, become mine, submit completely to me." 
 Colton FUCKIN Donavan...I dunno what to do with him. The prologue killed me. And then I went back and forth on my wonderful love-him-and-hate-him routine that I perfected during Driven. He is not an easy man to love, by any stretch of the imagination. But I will say having a glimpse at being inside his head was...helpful. Insightful. I liked it. Well, I didn't like it but...it was necessary to get to know why he does what he does. Being inside Colton's head was absolutely necessary in this book, there is no other way to hear and see some of the things that are needed, without being in his POV. You never knew when it was going to happen, it wasn't regular or routine, but it always made an impact. And understanding him more helped ease the pain on my heart just a little and okay...I'll admit it...I did love him more than I hated him. It's really impossible not to...even as exasperating as he can be. Until he did what I knew he was going to do and broke me just as quickly as he broke Rylee. 
 "I swear to God it's you!" 
 "Me?" I stutter flabbergasted. What did I have to do with what just happened? 
 "Mmm-hmm," he murmurs, staring at me intently. "I've never let my guard down. Never opened myself up to..." He shakes his head, his confusion and clarity written on his face. "I've been able to block things out for so long. Ignore emotions. Ignore everything, but you? You tear down walls I didn't even know I was building. You make me feel, Rylee." 
 Ace and Ryles...what can I say - don't read this book if you're of the faint of heart because it's a mother freakin angsty roller coaster of epic proportions. I'm happy, I'm sad, I'm ecstatic and then I wanna knee Colton in the balls (sound familiar? I said it in my Driven review too...I have a feeling that this is a reoccurring theme). I wanna fuck his brains out and then strangle him...yes, those familiar bi-polar crazy feelings are back in full force. I...was...all...over...the...place. I loved Rylee and Colton together...they're magic...they're this passionate burst of amazingness when they are together and happy. GOD BLESS AMERICA they are made for each other if that jack ass would just get it thru his head!!! GRRRR!!! (see...he's making me GRRR again!) I guess the part that makes me 'grrr' is the fact that Colton is his own worst enemy. There is one thing stopping Rylee and Colton from being amazing together...and that's Colton and his past. Not that his past isn't a minefield of fucked up and he has every right to feel the way he does but he's fucking up one of the few good things in his life and Rylee is SO amazingly awesome...I cannot fathom them not being together. And if he only knew how much Rylee could help him...if he only let her. 
 "Stop." His voice is stern, and I can't help but look up to meet his bemused eyes. "Look, I don't know how to explain it." His voice softens and he shakes his head. "I can't really. All I know it that with you, things were just different from the start. You broke the mold, Rylee." 
 There are a lot of skeletons that get revealed in this book...a few more from Rylee that I wasn't expecting and we start to see more and more from Colton and his horrible past, which obviously needed to happen. Badly. The only way for both of them to move forward is complete honesty...on both sides and I really liked that. And then Rylee goes and does something insanely stupid. I screamed, I cried, I stopped reading. The second I read it, I dropped my kindle and almost refused to continue. Because I knew what was going to happen next...and it did...and I cried more...and it sucked. For the next 25%+ it SUCKED. Ripped my heart out, stomped on it and drug me along for a painful suckville ride. It wasn't pretty...I didn't know if I was going to survive. 
 "Just remember what I always say; don't lose yourself trying to hold onto someone who doesn't care about losing you." 
 I love angsty books, I've said this over and over...and this part of the book was probably one of the most angsty books I've read. The entire time I am warring with myself because I know the truth, but I see Rylee's point and I'm CHEERING her on because she's being so smart and standing up for herself but at the cost of her fuckin spirit. She loves him so much. SO much it makes me tear up thinking about it. And I know he loves her, as much as his fucked up little heart can. Them together is brilliance written on paper and the torture of them being apart cannot be fully expressed in words. They're both shell's of the people they could be when they are apart...hence my total devastation. I just can't even begin to tell you the pain that was inflicted on my soul...I might never recover from it. It was beautiful torture but it still fuckin hurts. 
 '"I might not be able to tell you the things you need to hear with the traditional words you need to hear them in, but I swear to God, Rylee, I will try. And if I can't, then I'll show you. I'll show you with everything I have - anything it takes - where you place is in my life," he murmurs to me, shattering every last form of protection I have guarding my heart. 
 He just stole it completely. 
 And I just more than willingly handed it over.' 
 So after I've cried I dunno how many times, I'm just begging for someone to kill them or me or both...or maybe I'll just climb into the book and commit murder/suicide....thats when it happens. When the heaven's open up and I'm put out of my misery...I'm elated, thrilled, cloud mother fuckin' 9. HA! Yeah...that was short lived because then I get to the end and it's another freaking cliffhanger. NOT COOL Ms. Bromberg!!!!  The prologue in this book was really great. As soon as I read it, I felt like this installment of the series would be much more promising than the first. The first book was a huge disappointment in my eyes, with more flaws than anything else. The cliffhanger at the end made me decide to read on to see what happened next. 
 And to be honest, the first 40% of this book was marginally impressive. I felt like the authors writing had improved considerably since Driven. But as soon as I made up my mind that this book was in fact better, everything started falling apart. The dialogue between the characters was, again, so cheesy. People don't talk that way. I get it, you're trying to up the heat factor. But even the conversations between Rylee and Haddie, or Quinlan and Rylee... it was all just so ridiculous. It did not come naturally at all. 
 The gala where all the women in the state of California decided to verbally harass Rylee... I mean, really? Tawny, ok, fine. But five, six different women... no. It's overkill and no one believes that would really happen. Not even in fiction. I'm sorry, but it was absurd. And then Rylee overhearing the cliche conversation in the bathroom. I'm so beyond over that scenario. It's been done... and when it was done, it was done better. The dialogue in the bathroom, once again, was just silly. 
 Rylee, as much as I try to like the girl when I'm just hearing her inner monologue, was verging on pathetic in this book. I mean, I wanted to punch her. No one, I don't care how love sick you are, would put up with the stupid drama in this story. I love a controlling alpha male, broken and damaged from a childhood ridden with abuse and neglect... who grows up unable to open himself to love, and who acts out so as to push the female counterpart away. I love all that stuff. Do you know how I know I love that theme? Because it's been done and done and done again in other books. In this one, however, the delivery was so flawed, it just came off like a hot mess. 
 I think the last 30% of the book was the same old drawn out, redundant argument between Rylee and Colton. I mean, how many times can you beat a dead horse? Yes, high schoolers in juvenile relationships would continually talk in circles. Adults, especially a celebrity who refuses to commit, and a supposedly strong woman who is done taking his crap would not continue to have this ridiculous argument in a public place. Enough is enough. This series could possibly have been condensed into one long book if all the ridiculousness was cut out. 
 Cliche. That's all I kept thinking while reading. There were chunks of this book that I read before... in Beautiful Disaster. I distinctly remember Shepley telling Abby Abernathy that Travis would eventually do something catastrophic to their relationship and she'd need to push through it. That exact scenario was repeated in this book, but with Beck warning Rylee. And that's honestly just the top of the iceberg. 
 I really wanted to three star this book because it was, by degrees, better than the first. But I three star a lot of stories that I like and I don't think it'd be fair to group this book, as flawed as it is, with those other stories. I know this review is one of my more brutal takes on a story, but I can't justify a two star review without explaining myself.

sample_reviews.review_text: I don't care for paranormal storylines but since this book was written by my favorite author, I hoped it would be okay. I tried to stay with it but I just couldn't get past vampire scenes.

DNF at 62% - I just couldn't do it anymore. I really tried. I've had some issues with Kristen Ashley's books before, but never to the point I couldn't find one. I think it was the whole "breaking her" and "taming her" thing. You can't love her spirit and want to crush it at the same time. I tried to continue because I wanted to see where it was all leading... but no go. 
 I'll stick to the Rock Chick series since I'm enjoying that one!

** spoiler alert ** 
 I usually love Kristen Ashley's books, formula and all....though the formula becomes more obvious with each book. But I figured I love paranormals and I enjoy her alpha heroes, so I would give it a shot. I had a bit of trouble getting into the story at first, mostly because I wanted to hit Leah in the head too much (she reads like a much younger heroine - I was truly surprised she was 40) and the way that Lucien trapped her into their arrangement made me not like him for the first part of the book. The love scenes were still hot, but I really had trouble believing in their love because of the way they treated each other. I just had trouble connecting with Leah, and since a good portion of the book is from her POV...well, it hurt the narrative for me. I wanted more of a confrontation or danger for Leah at the end. The worldbuilding is very light, and it was a relatively easy read. I'm going to keep on with this series because even an "alright" book by this author is still enjoyable. I'm hoping the story and worldbuilding really ratchets up with the next book.

I almost feel embarrassed with the rating for this book. There have been a couple of books that were so so, but for them most part I really like this author, but this one was a big fail for me. 
 A large part of the reason why is Lucien and Leah. For the first half of the book Lucien was such an ass, he treated Leah like crap, didn't consider her views or thoughts. Even later when we learned more I didn't like him. I found his stalking of Leah for 20 years to be beyond creepy. And then there is his whole nickname for Leah of "Pet", don't even get me started on that. 
 Leah drove me nuts. I had a hard time remembering that she was 40 years old because she acted like a petulant teenager for most of the book. The way that she treated Lucien was just as bad as he treated her. 
 Even with all of my complaints there were some things that I liked. I liked Leah's family, liked their relationships and how they related to each other. Stephanie was funny and just the friend that Leah needed. Edwina was the perfect person to help settle Leah in her house and mother her. I also really liked Lucien's mother and kids, loved that they started out with reservations, but were quickly won over to the couple's relationship. I finally really got interested in the story when Gregor revealed his secret. Until this point I had no desire to read any more in this series, but with the knowledge I want to know more.

 I don't usually admit this but I'm a pretty huge fan of vampire books. And having read about a million (obviously I'm being dramatic) I felt like this one just didn't make the cut. Don't hate me for saying this but I didn't like the writing or the way the story was told. It felt stunted and confusing and although I'm all for fancy old talk making the vampires seem more authentic, the language in this had me re-reading sentences and saying 'huh?' 
 I do think the world building was good but I wanted to know so much more. I needed details and history and all I got were snippets, and being that one of the main reasons I stuck this book out until the end was for details and history, I was not a happy reader. 
 I did like the character development and the characters themselves. Leah's personality was great to read and I'm a sucker for an alpha male so Lucian ticked the right boxes. BUT (I know, I'm really picking at this now, eh?) however much I liked Leah I couldn't accept that she was a 40 year old woman. No 40 year old woman I have ever known behaves so immaturely. Hell I'm 23 and half my friends are more mature half the time. It just didn't sit right with me. 
 I did enjoy the final few chapters when everything came together but in the end I was left feeling like I'd only read half a book, and uncomfortable with the characters.

 "Her eyes narrowed. "You know, Lucien, you need to make up your mind. Either you're this guy or you're the jerky, controlling guy who I met at The Selection or you're the near-miss murder guy last night. Pick one. I'm getting confused."

 "He spoke them as vow. 
 "Until the sun falls from the sky."

 Unlike his commanding declaration, when she spoke she spoke only to him.

 "The instant he got us in this position, before I processed I was in it and therefore was by no means ready for what he was going to say next (not that I ever would be), he stated, "I'm in love with you, sweetheart." 
 Oh my God!

I love Kristen Ashley's writing. Whenever I'm in the mood for that alpha male hero - even if they are just shy of being an anti-hero, or, in this case, if they are a centuries old vampire, I know that I can count on Kristen to provide that character. She does not disappoint with Lucien, and in fact, really delivered a new type of Vampire for me to love. I'm not an avid paranormal reader, so I don't know if my standards are as high as others that consider that their main genre, but Lucien is definitely one to remember. 
 This story starts off with Leah attending her Selection. Her family has been offering its members up, for generations, to be concubines to Vampires. This was an agreement settled upon between vampires and mortals in order to provide some type of order and rule to Vampires feeding off of humans. Leah is not happy about her fate, and she has further tried to avoid that fate by continuing to be in a relationship since coming of age, as they will not take a man or woman from a known relationship. So, this is another factor that I liked about Leah - she was 40 and not that young, naive female character that does not know her mind. 
 Lucien, who is somewhat of a legend among his people, has been waiting for Leah since she came of age to be in a Selection, so everyone knows that she belongs to him. Everyone except for Leah, that is. She fights this for weeks, which Lucien actually appreciates and looks forward to, as he feels that the agreement has taken away something elemental from Vampires - the ability to hunt and "tame" a mate of their choosing. So, without asking anyone, Lucien actually creates a different type of arrangement with Leah, and this sets off a domino effect within the world of Vampires, as well as other Immortals. It actually begins a set of Prophecies, although more is to be revealed in the coming books. 
 As for Lucien and Leah, there are many among Lucien's kind that are against Lucien having the type of relationship with Leah that he wishes to have, so they set about making life difficult for Leah, as she is the most fragile of the two. Lucien finds out that he has more people supporting him, however, than he realized, but he has to find out who he can and can't trust before Leah is hurt.

There are two ways to read this book. One way is to listen when Ashley speaks via her hero and says 'Don't judge this by human morals.' She makes it clear that this vampiric species is humanity's natural predator and that the concubine/vampire relationship is actually a form of protection for the human race. Since the concubines provide food for the vampires and are protected by the tenets of vampiric culture, vampires aren't allowed to go hunting for humans. Looked at in this way, the concubine/vampire relationship, on paper, makes sense. However, the other way to read this book is with human morals. If you look at Lucien's and Leah's relationship with ideas like 'free will' and the right to say no in mind, it's rather disturbing. With regards to Leah, the thought of Stockholm Syndrome came to mind at several points and if I'd be in Leah's exact shoes, I'm pretty sure I would have gone catatonic. 
 I was perpetually straddling the line between objective reader and outraged woman. If Ashley were to strip this story of all its paranormal elements, Lucien would be so far from a hero, it's not funny. He stalks her for years, forces her to sign herself into indentured servitude, isolates her from her friends and family, strips her of her ability to choose, and is borderline emotionally/physically abusive. Ashley even admits in the book that if the vampire Ruling Council found out that Lucien forced Leah into the contract, he'd be punished. So, in that respect, you can't claim it's a cultural thing because even the vampires think it's wrong! 
 I do think this was one of Ashley's strongest examples of world-building. If she had chosen to go more of a 'marriage of convenience' route, where Leah knew what she was getting herself into, it would have been a much stronger book. Lucien, despite being his asshole tendencies, was a consistent character. He never changed who he was, but as Leah fell in love with him (I still don't understand why), the stronger connection to her made him dial back the asshole-ness. Leah, on the other hand, was all over the place. She's forty-years old, but has the maturity level of a twenty-year old. She's strong-willed and she makes some monumentally bad decisions. If she hadn't gotten expelled from Vampire Studies, she would have known her contract was unusual and she could have been free of Lucien right away. She was a media specialist, for cripes sake. Maybe that means something different in the UK, but for me, that means she was a school librarian and nobody knows the power of information more than librarians. 
 I'd given Until the Sun Falls from the Sky three stars, but after writing all this, I'm dropping it down to two. I'm going to read the next book when it comes out because it's werewolf/human so I'm hoping Ashley will avoid creating another Lucien.

I've been delaying starting this series (and the Fantasyland series) for a while now. I don't usually like paranormal stories, but I'm kind of obsessed with Kristen Ashley's other stories so I wasn't sure what to expect with this book. I think that the letdown came in comparing this to other KA books. In my opinion, it's just not as good as some of my favorites by her. Having said that, I did enjoy this more than I would probably any other paranormal romance. I really liked the world building that was started in this book, and I will definitely be reading the rest of this trilogy. 
 First of all, I'm still not sure about my feelings for the main characters. Lucien was somewhat redeemed in the last quarter or so of the book, but until then he drove me nuts. I think he could've worked a little harder to cut Leah some slack. It's difficult enough being uprooted from your family and friends or moving to a new place if it's your own choice, but add in the fact that she was forced to sign that contract and, oh yea, her new bf she just met for the first time is an 800 year old vampire. She was pretty much doomed for failure. And speaking of Leah, 40 years old, really? She acted like a teenager for a pretty good chunk of the story and honestly was treated like one by Lucien and her family. Maybe if they had spoken to her about the situation like an adult she would have behaved more like one. Hmm, guess we'll never know. 
 Overall, I liked the story more than I expected. I think that KA did a good job with the world building by keeping things similar to reality and just changing some details. I also liked the way she approached the immortal characters as a whole. I liked seeing Lucien interact with his friends and children. I wish we could have seen a little more of Leah with her family or friends where she was more in her own element. The whole story was set in Lucien's world so it would have been nice to see how Leah acted if she were in more familiar surroundings, or to see how Lucien dealt with the tables being turned on him in that way. 
 Even though I'm only rating this with 3 stars, I would certainly call it a success by KA. If she hadn't been the author, I would have never given this book a second look. And now there's no way I'm going to stop before I finish the rest of the trilogy. Who knows? Maybe werewolves will be my immortal of choice.
This was an epic book. I should have read it before now. This is my first paranormal read in a year and I was not disappointed. I could not put it down. On to the next in the series.
Oooooh KA writes good vampires!!! Loved this.

No more books by this author for me. How she can write a really interesting hook and then follow it up with boring and lengthy stories is beyond me. 
 I hated Lucien and Leah - honestly pretty sure they hated each other as well. Somewhere around the last 1/3rd of this book it was like a switch flipped and despite all of the shit that they did (Lucien) to each other it was Insta Love.... 
 The sex scene every chapter did not help - repetitive and forced honestly. Along with this we are introduced to a handful of side characters that mean next to nothing since our author never explains them. Their actions don't make sense - the story doesn't make sense. 
 Kind of bummed I wasted days reading this.

DNF. 
 I've always at least LIKED Kristen Ashley's books. I like her Contemporary romances and i loved The Golden Dynasty. So i thought, eh why not? If she could write a vampire story anywhere near as good as she did her Fantasyland series then i was totally on board... 
 A hit... and a miss... Damn. 
 I mean, just 
 damn 
 . This book: i couldnt finish it. I just couldnt do it. I tried, I legitimately tried. It had the makings of a good Kristen Ashley books: great concept, interesting and well developed side characters, and a mystery that had me intrigued despite fully expecting/wanting a romance story. But the heroine is what inevitably did it for me. 
 She's forty years old, acts like a whiny teenager, and is TSTL even when given directions, a gps, and a fucking guide. 
 And that's pretty much the gist of why i DNF. To further my point, here's some of my thoughts as i started to read through the first few pages of the book(WARNING SPOILERS AHEAD): 
 1) First impression (first few pages): the heroine, Leah, is confusion personified. Despite her family literally being involved with vampires and this whole "concubine" business for generations. Was she REALLY told nothing for however many years she is (im guessing from her attitude late teens/early twenties??) Also on that note, why the FUCK has no one told her anything??? 
 2) Ok now i think she's just plain dumb. she disrespects a room full of vampires simply cause she doesnt know whats going on, which is dumb in itself. Instead of following someone else's lead (someone who- idk- UNDERSTANDS what's happening) she snaps and disrespects a room full of complete, total strangers. Strangers that could drain her dry without batting an eye. She even completely disregards some helpful- if not obvious- advice from a VAMPIRE, proceeds to think "im not dumb ill listen to her" and then low and behold COMPLETELY IGNORES SAID ADVICE. 
 3) I think Kristen Ashley is trying to make Leah out to be independent and "different" from the other girls but she just comes off whiny instead. Her internal dialogue is pretty much just: "but i dont wanna be a concubine" and "whats going on why wont anyone tell me anything wahhh" (I may be paraphrasing but you get what I mean). Its frankly annoying. She should have asked these questions BEFORE all this went down and instead it seems she's only NOW wondering whats going on. 
 (Also i think its just common courtesy to not be a frigid jerk when first meeting people. Even if you don't want to be there. It's called being an adult. Just food for thought) 
 4) I now know for a fact she's just plain dumb; she just revealed that she had all the chances to study up on vampires and a concubine's role she just choose NOT to. I mean, she doesnt have to like the situation but blatantly choosing to be ignorant is fucking asking to be put in shitty situations. Not to mention all her "questions" seem to be pretty fucking common knowledge and thus leads me back to: she could have learned about all this beforehand and been prepared. Just cause she refused to learn about it doesn't mean it would have gone away. Instead she's now just a catty, annoying heroine that im really not starting to like. 
 5) *LOUD GROANING* she's a super special snowflake; she's tall, pretty, has a body to die for, and comes from a prestigious family. idk what about her im supposed to sympathize with or even relate to except for maybe... yeh, no, i don't feel anything for her. She's just annoying tbh. (She's said she has redeeming qualities but honestly i've yet to see them) 
 6) Lucien has been introduced. He's crass and an ass and im loving it. let me bask in your hunky glory oh vampire overlord *bows down* 
 7) I've only just now noticed that Kristen Ashley has this fascination with clothing and tends to describe them to the reader, (me) when i could give two shits. I honestly dont care. She could be wearing a fucking burka and socks with dad sandals and I wouldn't even care/notice. Let's move one and not spend whole paragraphs on people's clothing please. 
 8)Leah's starting to piss me off. The times when she's SUPPOSED to fighting back and causing a ruckus, she's just sitting there doing nothing. Like when her mother and aunts had a copy of the Bonding contract, closed themselves in a room, and perused it for a whole hour without telling her jack shit. THAT'S when you start bitching and moaning about people not telling you stuff. NOT in the middle of a room full of vampires. Not to mention she just lets her family NOT tell her stuff, push her to do things she doesn't want to do at the threat of being disowned, and yet a vampire kindly asks her to not be stupid(aka NOT do something that would cause her death and other people trouble) and she gets all huffy???? dafuck. 
 10) IM DONE. Lucian just revealed that she's forty years old after berating her for not paying attention in vampire history class. She's being berated... at forty... for not paying attention in class and passing notes.... I repeat: she's fucking FORTY YEARS OLD and she acts like a fucking teenager. i just. i cant. i was willing to let a lot of her behavior slide had she been on the younger side. Then she'd just be a silly, young, easily prone to making mistakes youngster. But when she's a forty year old woman and she makes all the shitty choices a fucking teenager would make, its just embarrassing and sad. I mean, it doesn't mean she can't make mistakes but im pretty sure at forty she'd have SOME semblance of self preservation and maturity. But she doesnt. Which is worse imo. 
 This on top of the fact that for FORTY YEARS her family kept her in the dark about their vampire/concubine history made me nope so hard. I mean, what the fuck man?? You'd think if it was so "important" to your family you'd let your kids know before they hit fucking menopause jfc (not a bag on older women in romance books just a hit at how ridiculous it is that Leah's family kept it from her for so long). How did they even keep it from her for that long??? Generations- GENERATIONS- of her family have been concubines; lived and participated in this vampire/concubine society and she just didn't know?? What? No, seriously: What? 
 Ugh, i might try the other books in this series but this one? I give up.

Okay so this probably my least favorite Kristen Ashley title. 
 Color me crazy or hell, maybe I'm living in the land of rainbows and roses, but hero's should not ever ever never ever enjoy their heroines fear. Ever never! 
 It's just wrong. It is not the stuff, in my not so humble opinion, that hot guys are made of. 
 So the whole first part of this one was me being all kinds of annoyed/frustrated/pissed off at the hero. He gets better, but not by much. He blatantly lies to her! Grrr... I almost put this down a few times. But almost every other kristen Ashely review I've read all say the same thing...she cannot write a bad story( despite her many, many, many grammar issues ) So I persevered, and ending up not hating the book. 
 It was not a favorite, and won't ever be...I may not even read the next book in the three series, I disliked parts of this one so much. Plus the heroine...okay, heres the thing, but what works for the heroine in contemporaries does not work in pnr's...so Leah comes off as a pushover, weakling immature 40 year old. I kept waiting for her to be a little more kickass, a little less doormat. And while I loved the build up of the angst, for a PNR, it gets resolved waaaay to easily. 
 So somewhere between 2.5 and 3 stars... 
 With the addendum that I probably won't be able to keep myself from reading book 2, but if that ones as disappointing as UtSFFtS, then I'm writing off here pnr's and sticking to her moderns.

This review will be mostly about why I didn't give this one a Five S. You have all the usual awesome things: alpha huge guy falls for outspoken kinda cute tall woman (yes, this is a huge pro for me. Breath of fresh air not to have the h being a "petite, tiny, short" anything), fast paced, things-happening-packed, togetherness (even though sometimes reluctantly), HEA like no other, gorgeous sweet moments amidst really hawt ones, real-like second characters... A Kristen Ashley book, peeps , nothing new here. So, here goes my Justification Review: 
 To be completely honest, I'm not overly fond of supernatural-paranormal and whatever types of reads. In fact, if not for the reviews, highly recommended books and in all truth, the type of alpha men one can find in these books, I would not read the at all. In this case, also the fact that I was in a KA-kind-of-book-mood, and unfortunately she only has a limited line of contemporary stories, and one can only read a book so many times until you do need a new book. 
 So I grabbed this one. And as usual many emotions engulfed me. Sadly, at first, they were not very good. I love her jerky alphas, her outspoken heroines and the situations she puts them trough, the pace, the writing, the ambience, the things they say, the breaking points, the good, the bad, the ugly, and the beautiful, it all. With Until the Sun Falls From The Sky, however, I found myself thinking something was missing. 
 See, I think the error was the way this book was sold as. Or at least how I interpreted it. Or to be more specific, what wasn't said. You see, Lucien could easily be on our anti-heroes lists, our Douchebags-We-Can't-Help-But-Put-Up-With, Hawt-Hateful-Jerks, an others of the sort. Lucien was hard to like at first, there were too many things done and said that plain just, no-no. Not even because they happened, but because the communication was shit at the first half of the book. That's not to say I wasn't right along with Leah in most the ways she acted, and sadly also understood how she involuntarily reacted to him. But still, effing use words, people. 
 So what you trying to do to me 
 It's like we can't stop, we're enemies 
 But we get along when I'm inside you 
 You're like a drug that's killing me 
 I cut you out entirely 
 But I get so high when I'm inside you.. 
 But thank heavens, K.A. always makes me end up falling for her heroes. And I did. The second part of the book is much of the same except you understand a great deal more, you have much more wonderful Lucien to outweigh the bad, and everything just falls into place and I got my favorite type of comfort-read: the KA one; only with that heinous ~that turned up not to be so bad~, vampire twist. 
 The author also treats us to, what surprised me at first, a regular dual POV. And I loved it. Maybe this was what ultimately didn't allow me to hate Lucien, 'cause being in his head, well, you get to see behind what his 800 years of vampiretude has made him too obtuse to show and say. 
 I think all in all, what really put me off was the misunderstandings and miscommunications. -I'm not used to them, and I definitely don't like them. I rather have bombs, fights and cars exploding as long as the H&h are hand-in-hand, than to have them repeatedly turn on each other since they didn't come clean at the right time (or well, Lucien didn't). 
 But how could I not give this over four stars? 
 KA always goes straight to my heart (my imagination, my alpha lust, and quivering thingies), so kudos once again. After all, if I were ever to be with a vampire, I wouldn't do half bad if a Lucien-A-Like were to sweep me off my feet. Over all, really liked this.

There was no real relationship between the characters that would induce love. The situation can be describe as 2 vile words: slavery and rape. I am a big fan of Kristen Ashley. I love her contemporary romance novels because her heroes are all alpha males who tread the thin line between complete jerk and absolute alpha. I love her heroes because they do the most unbelievably annoying acts but say the most incredibly sweet things. I love how a lot of her books are about redemption, how they show that love truly defies odds and is worth all the trouble. 
 I haven't read The Three series because I really loved her contemporary novels that, in a selfish way, I did not want to read another genre from her. I should not have made that mistake. In fact, the moment that this first book from the series was available, I should have read it right away. The only good thing about my stupid decision was the fact that all three books have now been released for this series, so I can read them all right after each other instead of waiting for months and months for the next book to come out. 
 Until The Sun Falls From The Sky is a wonderful paranormal romance that is hot, sexy, and out of this world. It goes without a doubt that KA successfully creates communities, families, worlds with her series of books. In this book, however, she has gone way beyond the realms of realistic and contemporary fiction. She has created a world where mortals and immortals lived together, complete with laws, pacts, and history. 
 I am going to give this book four red hearts. The hero and the heroine were great together, when they weren't fighting. There were times when I felt that the part where he heroine kept fighting the hero was dragged out. However, after she gave in, everything was amazing until the book ended. Another thing I liked the least was that before Lucien mentioned that Leah was 40 years old, I completely thought she was only in her twenties. There was something truly immature about her thought process and the way she talked. 
 I will still say that this is definitely a great book because it leaves you with this yearning to get to the next book right away and find out of the three couples in the prophecy will be triumphant. Kristen Ashley truly does magic with her books, and yes, she can definitely write paranormal just as great as she does anything else.

This author is new to me I haven't ever come across her before friend here had recommended her writing. 
 I wasn't sure what to expect being new to this author and all but she didn't disappoint, the book is a story of a woman named Leah. Leah wants nothing to do with her families legacy she just wants to live her life her way, not with all these stuffy rules about being a vampires concubine. 
 Leah's life takes a few turns and before she realizes it she's exactly where she has no desire to be. She becomes what she never wanted to be flying anger in the face of tradition she's concubine but not willing to be anyone but herself and tradition can go fly a kite. She doesn't care if she was selected by "the mighty vampire Lucian" 
 Lucian is tall, dark, handsome and a vampire. He's someone even other vampires don't want to cross and he's got his work cut out for himself with Leah. He will change the game to have his victory, what he didn't plan on was losing his heart to a mortal spirited woman. 
 Leah is special and she doesn't know it she has abilities that couldn't have been known, needless to say this doesn't leave everyone happy. The governing body of vampire/mortal relations isn't happy either and Leah doesn't know about most of these things or what it might mean for her and her family. 
 When the enemy doubles and the decision gets closer will love be enough to protect her from enemies both seen and unseen? Will the mighty vampire Lucian meet his match in a mortal woman? 
 In this story; no matter how you deny it love will consume you, the question: is love enough to save you? 
 *I like the interaction between them I love her quick wit replies. 
 ** I didn't so much like that she forgave his lying ways so quick, I also found sayings/phases repetitive at the beginning and end of the story. 
 This book is a good read and surprised me on a consistent basis it wasn't another typical romance, yet it was, thanks Kristen Ashley for making the "The mighty vampire Lucian" 
 I would recommend this book if you like vampires, sarcasms, love stories 
 Favorite quote: 
 "you are forty years old" Lucian 
 "yes and I am not growing up until I am ninety three" leah

Link: http://lit4ladies.com/2013/10/13/favo... 
 Rating: 
 Until The Sun Falls From The Sky:(3 Teacups / 3 Handcuffs) 
 With Everything I Am:(5 Teacups / 4 Handcuffs) 
 Untitled: He's said one word, "MINE", we don't know his name, but we are already in love. 
 Our Thoughts: 
 KA does an excellent job at crossing mythologies. The first novel focuses on vampires, the second on werewolves. There is an overarching narrative woven throughout the series. It will bring the three main couples together to fullfill the prophecy and restore harmony to the races. 
 KA knows how to write hawt alpha males. Callum is one of our favorite book boyfriends, in both his human and wolf states. 
 Even though these men are mythological, they are still surprisingly normal. They fail to understand women, human or otherwise. A lot of the novels' conflict is the men's inability to understand their women and express their emotions. 
 These women are are strong and independent. They are not afraid to go head to head with their men. It takes awhile for them to truly be claimed. 
 These men aren't afraid to go against the customs of their kind to claim their mates. They will fight and die if anyone tries to separate them. 
 Like most KA novels there is a strong sense of family woven throughout the narrative. The characters discover that family isn't necessarily about blood, but those you love. 
 Neither vampires nor werewolves are villainized; like humanity they just have a few bad apples which makes the cultures more relatable. All the main characters want to do is live, find love and happiness! Who doesn't? 
 We can not wait for the last installment. We do not know much, but from the short snippet at the end of With Everything I Am, it holds great promise

reference_books.title: Seraphina (Seraphina, #1)
reference_books.review_text: I had higher expectations for this book, given the promise of the subject matter and all the rave reviews. It was a little disjointed and slow-moving for me, especially in the beginning. It picks up later. The writing is beautiful, the story is unique, and the series has potential. It just didn't have the quality I was looking for...the one where you bust out your iPhone kindle app every few minutes you get to sneak in a couple paragraphs.

reference_books.title: Cinder (The Lunar Chronicles, #1)
reference_books.review_text: I'm not sure why I disliked this one so much because the concept sounded like something right up my alley: a Cinderella story in a futuristic cyborg society set in New Beijing, complete with an alien race called the Lunars! But I think at the end of the day, I didn't feel any of the characters much, other than Cinder. They seemed a bit one-dimensional. I also saw things coming a mile away, and everything was a bit too predictable. I ended up skimming my way to the end.

reference_books.title: All Our Yesterdays
reference_books.review_text:
3.5 stars 
 I always love reading stories on time travel because it is interesting how authors choose to explain the phenomenon. And while I really enjoyed the action-packed story which kept me at the edge of my seat, I felt that the science fiction element was a bit lacking. I still don't particularly know how time travel "paradoxes" work, nor do I completely understand how altering the past doesn't completely change the future. However, that wasn't the point of this story, and the author used time travel as a means of illustrating other concepts. If you could go back in time, how would you view yourself? If you could look into the future, how would you feel about who you become? What if "fixing" what is wrong with the now involved going back to kill the one person you loved? Could you do it?

reference_books.title: Eat, Pray, Love
reference_books.review_text: So boring. I was hoping to come out of this (since I'm also going through a divorce) with some awakening and insight, since I am planning an around the world trip soon and will be going wherever the wind takes me. Instead, I found this a bit cliche and boring as hell. Struggled to get through this. Narrator: uninteresting. Side characters: uninteresting. World and atmosphere: uninteresting. What this whole thing felt like was a stream of consciousness from some lady that I really did not care about, and the words were pretty much irrelevant to me, regardless of the fact that I read it because I thought it would be relevant to my life situation and I thought I could relate. I kind of equate it to listening to your very talkative friend talk at you about herself, and you wish she'd stop so you can get a word in, but she just won't. Left this book with absolutely nothing to take away.

reference_books.title: Fifty Shades of Grey (Fifty Shades, #1)
reference_books.review_text: Ok, I put this off as long as I could and then I just needed to find out what all the hype was about. The good: sex scenes. The bad: the writing, the storyline, the characters, and just about everything else. 2 stars means it was ok... I thought it was a very gutsy and colorful book on a topic that is "taboo" (BDSM) and I appreciated it for that.

 I loved this series so far, but I did not love this book. In this book, she switches between points of view for almost ever chapter, and this is something I really don't like, something I hated about Game of Thrones. And the whole book dragged...it was very slow until probably the later part of it...which actually ends up being quite good. But it didn't work...for me.

So much happens in this book, there was SO much amazing character growth and it happens to be a GREAT setup for the next. Sorscha also turned out to be incredibly brave even though I did NOT like her relationship with Dorian. I still ship Celaena and Dorian for the end! They'd SERIOUSLY be this incredible power couple. They could unite their kingdoms. She has fire and he has ice! Not to mention the dialogue between Rowan and Celaena when he said, "'Sometimes, mates can be together intimately before the actual bond snaps into place.' 'It's a useless hope to cling to, anyway.' 'Do you want the truth?' She tucked her chin into her tunic and closed her eyes. 'Not tonight.'" Dorian and Celaena have been together intimately in some ways and maybe the REAL bond just hasn't happened yet. There was a connection between them though and they're like a present day Elena and Gavin. I REALLY hope they happen... UGH... it's all so great! I'm really looking forward to the Aelin and Aedion reunion that will hopefully happen and I really really really want Dorian to be freed of his dad's dark collar. That was one of the craziest parts of the book and I totally didn't see it coming. On the bright side he isn't dead and all hope isn't totally lost. I think Celana cares enough about him to try to redeem who he used to be. All in all, I'm anticipating the next book to read how this plays out.This series is arguably THE BEST YA FICTION I've ever read. Like I said in another review its a great mix of action, adventure, romance, fantasy and mystery. And on a side note... this book slightly reminds me of LOTR because she wants to retrieve the Wyrdkeys and put them into the gate in order to keep their power from access like Frodo and Sam wanted to bring the ring to Mordor.

Definitely my least favourite of the series that I've read so far. Absolutely loved the first half! It was action packed and I loved the story. However, story started to slow down and so did my reading. It took FOREVER to get through the second half. Also, the second half failed to keep me entertained and at the last 100 pages I found myself skimming chapters. I did enjoy all the new characters that were added though, especially Manon and Rowan and Aedion (I guess all of them really). I do have high hopes for the fourth book which I ought to pick up.

I can't. I just don't even know what to say. I mean my initial thought when I could form one was "What the heck did I just read???". No joke I sat on a super uncomfortable concrete bench for like 2 minutes with my eyes wide and my mouth hanging open because...WHAT THE HECK DID I JUST READ???!!! 
 I'm not going to go into a description this book. What I say wouldn't really give it any justice. But what I will tell you is that Heir of Fire is very different from the other two books and I had a whole host of emotions going through me when reading it. I had read Throne of Glass and Crown of Midnight pretty close to reading Heir of Fire so I expected something similar to the two. But that is not what Heir of Fire was. As one of my blogging friends said to me, this is Celaena's book. And I couldn't agree more. But because of that I had trouble when I first started reading this one. It was on the verge of being 4 stars. I know, GASP! But as I progressed further into the book, the book was pushed up to 4.5 stars level. And then when I read the last heart pounding 60 pages it was cemented as a solid 5 star read. Let me tell you why: 
 4 Stars: The new characters flustered me. After reading Throne of Glass and Crown of Midnight pretty much back to back, I was used to a certain setting with certain people. Heir of Fire threw that comfort out the window. There was more magic than I expected, an added level of enemies that was hinted at in Crown of Midnight, and just plain more people. I had trouble connecting to the newbies when I craved my trio. 
 4.5 Stars: Celaena started to grow and not be so mopey and whiny. In the first two books Celaena was this powerhouse that had no fear. She was so strong. But she was changed in Crown of Midnight and that change carried over into the beginning of Heir of Fire. At first it was not a change I liked. And then the book started to grow and take shape and Celaena started to find herself again. She stopped being stuck in her land of self-pity and became the warrior, the champion, we all love her to be. 
 5 Stars: THE END. The fantastic flipping ending! That is really all I have to say. This book could have been a 2 star read throughout the whole story and I would give it 5 stars because of that freaking ending! I can't even comprehend that ending. Maas blew all her other books out of the water with that ending. (Hmm...how many times can I say ending in one paragraph???) 
 So basically all I can really say about Heir of Fire is that it is an amazing roller-coaster of emotions and growth and action and heartbreak. I cannot stress enough to not go into this book expecting things to be the same as they were in Crown of Midnight. Now that I am removed from the book I can see why things changed and why Heir of Fire was different. It's because life changes. There are always new obstacles and we have to deal and move on and Maas clearly got her point across on this one. As it was said in a discussion with two other book bloggers, Heir of Fire is very much Celaena's book and I now feel closer to her after reading it. 
 Give me more Ms. Maas, GIVE ME MORE!

Heir of Fire. 
 This is a shame. I have wanted to get into a fantasy series that was more magic driven than Game of Thrones for awhile now. Sadly, that isn't happening for me with Heir of Fire. This book is part of the promising Throne of Glass series. It features a female assassin, a rugged Captain of the Guard, and a Prince who is hiding illegal magic. All of this should make for a very fun book, especially since the 2nd one left me on such a high note. . Crown of Midnight was so good, I could not help but put it onto my Top Ten books of 2016 list, but then I read the 3rd book. 
 Perhaps tried to read the third book would be more accurate. This is my 3rd or 4th attempt to read it but I just can't do it. Why? Well, I think it is because of the world building. There is just too much of it. We get introduced to so many different elements that were not there before that this book feels like a different one entirely from the first two books. I heard from the booktube grapevine that Maas had to stretch this series into six books, and with this one, it shows. We get long tides of text telling us about this world that we should be seeing, but, all the while, I just kept wondering why I should care. These elements do not feel as well integrated into the universe that Maas supposedly built. This leads us from one boring exposition dump about X element in Y land, but I just...did not...care. 
 This boring exposition bleeds into the character POVs as well. We switch between many alternative POVs that should be exciting, with political betrayals, enemies gathering on the horizon, and characters going through personal inner struggles. Sadly, the exposition gets in the way. We go to one POV that begins very dry, explaining some exposition about the world, then, as soon as things get exciting, we switch to another POV, and the dull exposition starts up again. This excitement roller coaster did not help me find these characters endearing and I just can't help but put the book down. 
 I have to give this book a two out of five. I am one of those people who wonder why I should keep reading a series I hate when I could be reading something better that is by a not as famous author? Since the next book in the series, according to the reviews on Goodreads, is similar in the relationship between the excitement and the boredom, I think I'll leave the series here.

A court to change the world. 
 Wow wow wowowow. 
 I was hesitant about beginning this book because so many people loved it and I was scared I wouldn't, but wow. Heir of Fire is fantastic. Sarah J. Maas continues to improve installment after installment. I think this book is my favorite out of the three so far, mainly because Aelin and Rowan *sigh. And Aelin in general. She is just perf. 
 Celaena is in a bad place at the beginning of the novel. She's beat down, her soul is spent, and her hope extinguished. She blames herself for what's happened so far, beating herself over the head with it. And it sucks seeing her like this, but that's what makes her recovery so satisfying to watch. It's what makes her triumphs so glorious. 
 I love stories about training and seeing the process in which heroes go through to become so great. I like reading about their motivations, their ups and downs, their struggles-- everything. If you don't like doing so, the first half of this book will bore you, as it has for some. But if you enjoy that kind of stuff, great! Read this now. 
 As for the witch's point of view in this novel, I didn't care for it much, but I'm interested in seeing her relationship with Aelin. I liked her spunk and determination and I'm excited for scenes of her and Aelin together. Yesss. 
 Rowan Rowan Rowan. Is it too much to hope for a loveline between him and Aelin? Gah. I loved his character and how he could meet Celaena blow by blow, retort by retort. He is brutal and has his own issues and darkness, that seeing him and Aelin together-- they're a formidable pair. 
 In my heart, I'm still stubbornly hoping for a Dorian + Celaena ending, but come on, we all know it's going to be Chaol. No doubt about it (though I don't really know how I feel about him anymore. I kind of honestly don't care about what happens to him?). Let's just hope he doesn't die in the process. Let's hope none of them die in the process (foolish, I know) (Dorian at the end of the book, though. sobs.). 
 Overall, Heir of Fire was touching at times, intensely satisfying at others, and just so so good. I can't wait for the next one. Please come quickly. 
 p.s. who else is excited about the possible lineup for Celaena's court???! Chaol, Aedion, Manon, Rowan, Dorian-- I just can't. I'm so excited.

The majority of this sizable third installment in the Throne of Glass series is spent on Celaena coming to terms with the events of Crown of Midnight and embracing her destiny as a power player in the war to come against Adarlan. And by majority, I mean 450 pages of guilt ridden internal debates, training, and more guilt ridden internal debates. Celaena's journey is interspersed with glimpses of the burgeoning rebel movement in Rifthold and a previously unknown witch, whose importance is still a bit of a mystery. The scope and breadth of the story expands significantly with a larger cast of characters, more backstory, and more horrors and evil plotting from the monstrous King of Adarlan, promising some truly epic events to come. For the most part, Maas holds it all together and weaves a tale of redemption, love, and the true meaning of power but because of the length I lost interest here and there. The last 100 pages of Heir of Fire are truly action packed with some surprising twists and hints of the epic-ness to come. The problem is those events are still to come and whether the 450 page set-up was strictly necessary is debatable. Although the book doesn't end on a cliff-hanger there is still a pretty bold faced "To Be Continued.." much like Crown of Midnight. A long-winded but essential milestone in the Throne of Glass journey.

 That said, Manon is reasonably decent as a character, and some of the other characters are interesting. The writing needs to actually have Mary Sue (and most of the characters frankly) actually FIGHT and WORK to gain things, rather than it just being an 'ohh, no,,, I cannnnnn't I need to whingeeeeee, emotionsss.... but oh wait.... I'm like, the BEST assassin/Mage/special person everrrrrrrr' and then winning. In a lot of ways, it reads like the sort of games you play as a little kid, whereby it's just 'the bad guy appears! He kills bunch of canon-fodder people, and/or the character created for the sole purpose of emotional trauma, and then the main characters kick his ass with no effort because they're all suuuuuch badasses!'
